chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:
There is no one who is tested -- even if his test is severe -- who is more rightful to supplication than the one who is in well-being, who is not safe from being tested.

key_terms.ابتلي: To be tested, tried, or afflicted by God as a means of spiritual examination
key_terms.البلاء: Test, trial, affliction; can refer to both good and bad tests from God
key_terms.الدعاء: Supplication; calling upon God in prayer and entreaty
key_terms.المعافى: One in a state of well-being, health, and safety from affliction
key_terms.بلوى: Trial, tribulation, or affliction sent as a test of faith

ai.seo_question: Who is more in need of supplication: the one who is tested or the one who is well?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) teaches that those who are currently healthy and well have a greater need for supplication (du'a) than those already afflicted, because the healthy person is never safe from trials that may come at any time. This teaching was delivered to encourage the faithful to be proactive in seeking God's protection, recognizing that well-being is a temporary blessing that can change at any moment.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Musa al-Khashab from Ghiyath b. Kalub from Ishaq b. `Ammar from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: `Ali (as) would say:
There is not one who is tested – even if his test is severe – who is more rightful to supplication than one who is well, who is not safe from being tested [at any point].
